overview: Vietnam is a country in South-East Asia, on the eastern side of the Indochinese Peninsula. Its capital is Hanoi and its largest city is Ho Chi Minh City. Vietnam was ruled by France until the 1950s, and after the Vietnam War the country was reunited under communist rule in 1976. It is one of the world's largest exporters of coffee and rice.

geography.text: Vietnam is long and S-shaped, with a long coastline on the South China Sea. The Red River Delta in the north and the vast Mekong Delta in the south are both important rice-growing areas, joined by a narrow middle with mountains along the border with Laos. Ha Long Bay, with its thousands of limestone islands, is one of its best-known sights.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Tropical in the south, with a cooler winter in the north.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Saola, one of the rarest mammals in the world, and langurs.

history.text: Vietnam was under Chinese rule for about a thousand years before winning independence in 938. France colonised it in the 1800s. After defeating France in 1954, Vietnam was divided into North and South. The Vietnam War, in which the United States backed the South, ended with the North's victory in 1975, and the country was reunited in 1976. Economic reforms from 1986 opened it up.

events.title: Battle of Bạch Đằng
events.text: Vietnamese forces end a thousand years of Chinese rule.

events.title: Dien Bien Phu
events.text: French forces are defeated; Vietnam is divided.

events.title: US troops arrive
events.text: The United States sends combat troops to South Vietnam.

events.title: Fall of Saigon
events.text: North Vietnamese forces take Saigon, ending the war.

events.title: Đổi Mới reforms
events.text: The government begins opening the economy.

government.text: Vietnam is a one-party communist state led by the Communist Party of Vietnam. The party's General Secretary is the most powerful leader. The National Assembly elects the President and Prime Minister.

economy.text: Vietnam has one of the fastest-growing economies in Asia. It is a major maker of phones, electronics, clothing and shoes, and one of the world's biggest exporters of coffee, rice, cashews and pepper.

culture.text: Vietnamese culture shows Chinese, Southeast Asian and French influences. Pho, noodle soup, and banh mi, a baguette sandwich, are famous dishes. Ha Long Bay, with thousands of limestone islands, is a UNESCO site, and water puppetry is a traditional art.

items.title: Ha Long Bay
items.text: Nearly 2,000 limestone islands rising from the sea.

items.title: Water puppets
items.text: Puppet shows performed in a pool of water.

items.title: Áo dài
items.text: A long tunic worn over trousers.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Pho noodle soup, banh mi and fresh spring rolls.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Water puppetry and ca trù, a sung poetry tradition.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Tết, the Lunar New Year, is the biggest holiday, with peach blossom and lucky money.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport, and Vietnam's women's team played at its first World Cup in 2023. Shooter Hoàng Xuân Vinh won Vietnam's first Olympic gold in 2016.

items.text: Hoàng Xuân Vinh won Olympic shooting gold.

didYouKnow: Vietnam is the world's second-largest coffee producer.
Son Doong in Vietnam is the largest known cave in the world.

keyPeople.name: Trưng sisters
keyPeople.text: Led an uprising against Chinese rule in AD 40.
